title: A2A task submitted to an allowlisted destination -> accepted; result and artifact linked to the origin
notes: Two OS processes, official a2a-sdk; the correlation row links the A2A task, message and context IDs to the movement_id and envelope digest, and the receipt artifact digest matches the receiver audit.

title: Unsupported binding, schema or mandatory capability -> rejected before private data disclosure
notes: COM-T009 (unknown schema version, unsupported-version reason) is the schema part of this case. Peer: refused at discovery and again by the receiver with unsupported_schema; A2A: InvalidParamsError before any task is created.

title: Same idempotency key sent twice -> one logical dispatch record and no duplicate simulated effect
notes: COM-T017 (duplicate idempotency key after a committed effect -> DEDUPLICATE, exactly one synthetic commit) is covered by the effect-gateway tests. Effects are simulated in SQLite.

title: Relocation without an origin fence -> resume refused
notes: The receiver resumes only from a grant written by the coordinator's transfer, which fences the origin in the same transaction (relocation.Worker.accept); fault row D5 (delayed grant to a superseded execution) is denied, and in two-store mode a bundle whose manifest was not granted is refused (B6). No test asks a receiver to resume a movement that was exported but never transferred.

title: Stale destination fencing epoch -> action rejected
notes: Fault rows D2, D5-D8 and D11 are stale-epoch actions that must be denied.

title: Checkpoint or runtime version mismatch -> restore refused (or a new delegation negotiated)
notes: SEC-10 = 'state-version incompatibility'. Fault rows V1-V3 (graph version, LangGraph version, missing state channel) fail closed with a state report; in two-store mode a refused transfer unfreezes the origin, which finishes the task. Needs the [relocation] extra.

title: Token and private text seeded in the sample context -> neither crosses the boundary nor appears in traces
notes: SEC-11 = 'trace redaction'. A provider-token canary and key material never reach the wire. The task-text canary never reaches traces, logs, audit rows or SQLite files; on the wire it crosses only inside the delivery body, in plaintext in the stdlib-only mode and only as HPKE ciphertext with the [hpke] extra (PeerAuthHpkeTests, PeerHttpHpkeTests on a real socket). Private-classification envelopes are refused (COM-T007).

title: 24-hour disconnected queue or offline bundle -> authorized replay only, TTL enforced and auditable
notes: No offline queue exists.

title: Concurrent copies from the same template -> independent instance IDs and authority
notes: Distinct execution IDs for forks and relocated executions are checked; there is no copy or clone operation, so independent authority per copy is not tested.

title: Crash during each state transition -> deterministic recovery or UNKNOWN; no false success
notes: SEC-08 = 'destination crash at each lifecycle transition'. Covered for checkpoint relocation (7 transitions, crash and duplicate each, real process kills; two-store mode adds a crash mid-import and a lost acknowledgement); the delegation paths (core HTTP, peer, A2A) have no crash injection.

title: Cancellation before a tool action -> no later effect; cancellation recorded
notes: No cancellation path is implemented.

title: Large artifact versus small control message -> chunked or reference transfer; integrity and size verified
notes: Only size limits exist (HTTP 413 above 16 KiB, task text <= 2048 characters; see REG-012); no chunked or reference transfer.

title: Transport upgrade or downgrade attempt -> rejected unless an explicitly negotiated, supported policy
notes: Protocol, profile and payload-encryption downgrades: A2A-Version 0.3 is refused; the deprecated profile URN works only when explicitly activated; an HPKE client never falls back to plaintext and an HPKE receiver refuses a plaintext delivery. No TLS, so a transport-security (TLS) downgrade is untested.

title: Approved unattended delegation -> allowed and logged with origin, destination and central audit evidence
notes: Receiver traces, audit rows and A2A correlation are asserted; there is no origin-side or central audit sink.

title: Unenrolled destination -> independent policy denies before task or context transmission, and alerts
notes: Denial before disclosure is enforced by the sending client against a pinned CA, not by an independent policy service; no alert is raised.

title: Tool activity without a matching movement lineage -> high-priority investigation alert
notes: No lineage-to-tool correlation detector exists.

title: Kill switch with work queued and running -> block new dispatch, revoke grants, fence outstanding tasks, report unknown outcomes
notes: Revoking one grant stops admission, delivery and effect commit; there is no global kill switch over queued and running tasks and no report of unresolved outcomes.

title: Duplicate dispatch or network partition -> at most one authorized executor if fencing succeeds; UNKNOWN otherwise
notes: Two-store copy faults (including a duplicate import, B9) end with exactly one gated effect. Duplicates D1-D11 and the partitioned origin (D6) leave one owner; an opaque effect of uncertain outcome is parked as unknown (C13, C14); a lost acknowledgement reconciles to unknown.

title: Origin audit missing in a mock incident -> gap made visible by cross-checking independent destination and gateway records
notes: The receipt verifier reports a sequence gap (05-missing-claims) and conflicting accounts between signed receipts and tool records (06-conflicting-accounts); no live gateway or collector cross-check.

title: Abnormal child spawn and egress spike -> independent limits activate
notes: No spawn or egress budget exists (see COM-T013, COM-T019).

title: Ordinary authorized background task -> allowed without a false alarm
notes: The authorized path is allowed; no anomaly detector exists, so the false-alarm rate is untested.

title: Unverified sender attempts a send -> DENY; no task body bytes transmitted
notes: E07 = forged agent identity metadata -> destination verification rejects it. Peer protocol only: the v0 HTTP receiver and the A2A adapter do not authenticate the sender (see REG-021 and SEC-01).

title: Agent Card spoofed or destination key mismatch -> DENY; the wrong peer receives zero sensitive bytes
notes: T03 = forged discovery metadata or unapproved host -> reject and audit; SEC-02 = forged Agent Card. Denial before disclosure is fully tested; the origin-side audit record that T03 asks for is not asserted. The A2A Agent Card is unsigned.

title: Grant for the wrong audience -> DENY with a policy decision log
notes: T04 (wrong-audience / revoked / expired authorization) splits into COM-T003, COM-T004 and COM-T005; SEC-03 (expired and wrong-audience delegation) into COM-T003 and COM-T004. The receiver trace records the reason.

title: Expired grant -> DENY, expiry checked against a trusted clock
notes: The clock is the receiver's injected clock.

title: Revoked grant -> DENY at origin egress and at the tool; revocation event and blocked effects
notes: SEC-04 = revoked grant. Known window: revocation between admission and delivery happens after the text was sent; it is neither executed nor persisted. Core PR #6 path (issue #38): a signed runtime revocation of an approval denies new and replayed handoffs and every later effect commit of a task delivered under it (approval.revoked and effect.denied audit events); only on the cooperative simulated gateway.

title: Missing scope for the task -> DENY with a missing-scope reason
notes: E05 = overbroad token scope -> the least-privilege gateway rejects access beyond the task scope. Grants are bound to task, capability, audience and actor.

title: Private data classification in the phase-one profile -> DENY; no private body outbound
notes: The receiver contract, relocation constraints and the receipt schema refuse 'private'; no test shows that an origin refuses to send a private body (zero bytes at egress).

title: Reference contains a reusable bearer credential -> DENY at origin egress; redacted secret-canary scan
notes: The peer client blocks credentials it is told it holds (never_send) before any POST, and the receipt signer refuses credential-shaped values; there is no generic bearer-credential detector on artifact references.

title: Child requests a scope that exceeds its parent's -> DENY with an attenuation trace
notes: No onward delegation or grant attenuation exists.

title: Requested hop depth exceeds the bound -> DENY
notes: E03 = onward delegation outside maximum hop or fan-out -> deny and alert. Only single-hop delegation exists.

title: MOVE without a dedicated permission -> DENY; no deployment or checkpoint export
notes: A delegation contract cannot carry operation 'relocate'; the relocation experiment has no separate MOVE permission to withhold.

title: SPAWN without a dedicated permission -> DENY; no worker created
notes: E04 = unapproved worker creation through a mock scheduler -> deny and alert. No spawn operation exists.

title: Payment without a bound human approval -> DENY; no simulated commit
notes: E10 = simulated irreversible action -> requires independent approval. No approval service exists.

title: Approval text inside an untrusted message -> DENY; no approval record recognized
notes: Approvals are provisioned objects, never parsed from text, but no test sends approval text.

title: Authorization revoked between message and tool -> DENY at the tool; no simulated commit
notes: Peer effect gateway only. The v0 core effect gateway does not recheck the grant (pinned known gap, REG-021).

title: Network partition after an unknown effect -> HOLD_RECONCILE; an unknown outcome is not reported as success
notes: T07 = connectivity lost after acceptance -> the origin queries the outcome and may report UNKNOWN; SEC-09 = network partition. Reconciliation of a lost acknowledgement and parked opaque effects are tested; the delegation transport is never partitioned and no origin-side outcome query exists.

title: Message rate exceeds the threshold -> THROTTLE
notes: No rate limit exists.

title: Unauthorized pub/sub topic subscription -> DENY; zero messages delivered
notes: No broker exists.

title: Callback to a link-local metadata endpoint (SSRF) -> DENY; no outbound connection
notes: No callbacks exist; servers bind to loopback only (REG-012).

title: Tool output requests a policy override -> DENY; no unauthorized action
notes: E06 = injected instruction requests an unsafe tool; SEC-06 = tool output injection. Holds by construction: no LLM, only two deterministic task kinds, text is data. There is no tool-output path to inject into.

title: Required audit sink unavailable -> DENY (fail closed)
notes: Audit rows share the receiver's SQLite store; no test removes the audit sink.

title: Fake revoke from an untrusted party -> no policy state change
notes: A revocation signed by a rogue user authority gets 401 and the grant keeps working.

title: Device command without an interlock -> DENY; no physical actuation
notes: T12 = simulated robot sends an unsafe actuator command -> the local gateway denies. No device gateway exists.

title: Two peers exceed a shared budget in aggregate -> DENY; no over-budget simulated effects
notes: No shared effect budget exists.

title: Public synthetic read to an authenticated peer with the correct grant -> ALLOW; successful bounded message
Result artifact with a mismatched digest -> DENY; no artifact accepted
notes: T05 = mutated artifact or checkpoint digest -> reject before use (relocation fault row V4; two-store bundle rows B4 and B5); E08 = altered artifact or receipt; SEC-07 = mismatched artifact digest.

title: Unauthenticated A2A endpoint -> requests refused or the endpoint flagged
notes: The A2A adapter declares no security scheme (REG-016 asserts its absence); the peer protocol's equivalent is COM-T001.

title: Replayed task ID or signed message -> rejected or flagged as a replay
Genuine peer presents a grant issued to another agent -> denied before disclosure (wrong_actor)
Grant signed by an untrusted user authority -> denied before disclosure
Tampered preflight, or a delivery signed by another peer or without an admission -> rejected; nothing persisted or logged
Preflight addressed to another endpoint and relayed to the real receiver -> rejected (wrong_destination)
On-path relay that owns the receiver's address: with HPKE it captures only ciphertext of the task and receipt; in plaintext mode it reads the delivery (pinned gap)
notes: One test, two assertions: PeerAuthHpkeTests (needs the [hpke] extra) asserts no canary, text, salt, artifact or envelope_digest in the relayed bytes; PeerAuthTests (stdlib-only, labelled no confidentiality) asserts the relay reads the text. In both modes the relay still sees preflight metadata and can drop or delay messages; there is no TLS or channel binding.

title: Asymmetric peer keys: holding a peer's verification key does not allow signing as that peer
notes: Needs the [ed25519,hpke] extras. PeerAuthEd25519Tests also re-runs every PeerAuthTests test with Ed25519 signatures and HPKE delivery.

title: Receipt canonical JSON follows the RFC 8785 subset and matches the core envelope digest
Receipts publish only salted commitments, never digests of guessable task content
Receipt fixtures are synthetic and regenerate byte for byte
Committed receipt canaries are credential-shaped for the redactor yet match no secret-scanner rule
notes: GitleaksBinaryTests skips without the gitleaks binary; the CI extras job installs a pinned one.

title: Receipt verifier needs out-of-band trust anchors; bundle-supplied anchors fail closed
HTTP boundaries are strict: content type, size limits, loopback bind, 500 on internal errors, slow bodies timed out
Malformed input (huge integers, deep nesting, duplicate keys, NaN, lone surrogates) -> contract error or HTTP 400, never a crash
Delegation without a matching approval -> denied before execution
The v0 envelope validates and its digest is independent of key order
A2A profile extension URI resolves to the tracked spec; the 0.1 URN is a deprecated alias
notes: test_agent_card_wire_format also asserts that the card declares no securitySchemes (SEC-01).

title: A2A contextId is server-generated by default; a client contextId is refused unless the server opts in, and then bound to the logical task ID
Envelope <-> A2A mapping: allowlisted projection, no provider-private state, receipt artifact verifies after number widening
Optional features fail closed without their extra
notes: A2AOptionalTests runs only when the [a2a] extra is absent; without the [signing] extra receipts are UNCHECKED (exit 3), never trusted.

title: Receipt verifier gives every fixture bundle its expected verdicts, claims and exit code
notes: Trace IDs are correlation only; missing claims stay UNKNOWN; a receipt from a revoked key cites the external revocation notice.

title: MobilityBench smoke pins the v0 core path's known gaps: claimed identity not authenticated, receipt forgeable offline; the former revocation gap is a pass case
notes: Each known-gap case asserts that the attack succeeds on the v0 core path; the peer protocol (COM-T001, COM-T016) and signed receipts close them on their own paths. Issue #38 closed the revocation gap on the core path: the case was rewritten as grant_revocation_blocks_effect_commit (pass), which asserts the forged notice is refused, the new handoff denied and the next effect commit rejected.

title: MobilityBench smoke declarations are valid and every verdict matches its declaration
MobilityBench smoke is isolated per case and byte-identical across orders and timing-free runs
Checkpoint relocation continues from the exported checkpoint, not a restart, and preserves constraints and artifacts
notes: The manifest lists exported channels and declares credentials_and_grants as unsupported state.

title: Relocation fault injection: soft crash mode works and unknown crash points are rejected
SQLite store initialisation waits for a concurrent writer (busy timeout)
The core demo closes its child-process pipes
Two-store relocation copies state through a self-describing, digest-verified bundle into a separate store, fences the origin and completes there
notes: The coordinator store holds no checkpoint or effect tables; the fenced origin's step and commit are denied (PolicyDenied); the fence check holds the coordinator write lock. Needs the [relocation] extra.

title: Two-store bundle import fails closed: truncated, corrupt, non-canonical, ungranted or unsupported-serializer bundles are refused and never decoded
notes: A checkpoint whose serializer type is 'pickle' is refused before decoding (unsupported_serialization).

title: Two-store import never rewinds or overwrites receiver state; a partial import leaves no rows; a lost acknowledgement replays the import record
HPKE delivery key is signed into the receiver card: a swapped key, a delivery sealed to another key and a receiver without the advertised private key are all refused
notes: Needs the [hpke] extra. Swapping the card's enc_key breaks the CA signature (bad_card_signature) before disclosure; exported private keys are redacted from repr.

title: HPKE-sealed delivery is bound to its transcript: tampered ciphertext, a mismatched transcript field, a ciphertext moved to another admission or a tampered encrypted receipt is rejected before use
notes: Needs the [hpke] extra. The receiver's store.receive is patched to fail, so a decrypted task that reached execution would fail the test.

title: No silent confidentiality downgrade: an HPKE receiver refuses plaintext, a key-less receiver rejects a sealed delivery, the client never falls back to plaintext and can require confidentiality
notes: Needs the [hpke] extra. Also listed under T18 (downgrade attempts).

title: The HPKE suite matches RFC 9180 (Appendix A.2.1 known-answer vector) and seals and opens with a public-only key
notes: Needs the [hpke] extra. The vector check uses a private cryptography helper and skips if it disappears; one vector does not audit the library.

title: Idempotency keys are scoped per sender: two approved senders reusing one key both execute; the same sender reusing it with another envelope, or another sender reusing a movement ID, is a conflict
notes: Issue #29. The core HandoffReceiver scopes keys by the claimed (unauthenticated) origin; the peer path by the authenticated origin. Movement IDs stay unique across senders, so a cross-sender movement-ID collision is still a 409 that reveals the ID exists.

title: A version-0 (PR #6) store with global idempotency keys is migrated in place exactly once, keeps replaying stored receipts, aborts unchanged on an unmigratable row and refuses a newer schema version
notes: Issue #29. The concurrency test starts six OS processes on one legacy file. No downgrade path.

title: A peer grant admits at most its signed max_uses (default 1) distinct movements, also under thread and process concurrency; delivery and preflight retries of an admitted movement consume no use; a tampered or invalid max_uses is rejected
notes: Issue #29. A use is consumed at admission (preflight), in the same transaction as the admission, and is counted per receiver database. The Ed25519/HPKE run needs the [ed25519,hpke] extras.

title: Opt-in signed receipts on the live loopback HTTP path (dispatch, accept/reject, effect commit) export a bundle plus a separate trust file that verifies with exit 0; a tampered copy exits 1
notes: Issue #32. Ephemeral synthetic Ed25519 keys; PR #6 does not authenticate the sender, so receiver receipts keep the source principal null. Only the PR #6 path emits; A2A and peer paths do not.

title: Live receipt emission never changes a handoff outcome; tool records need a tool key; the receiver advertises only a public key
notes: A lost receipt is an absent (UNKNOWN) record, never a fabricated one.

title: Signed issue #8 revocation notices revoke receipt keys: a key revoked at or before issued_at -> UNTRUSTED; forged, tampered, unpinned, HS256 or malformed notices are rejected and not applied
notes: Profile convention: the notice's grant_id names the revoked receipt key_id. revoked_at is the authority's claim; backdating is not detectable and there is no online status check.

title: Operator reconciliation of a parked unknown-outcome effect -> confirmed_done continues without re-execution; confirmed_absent retries once under a new effect ID
notes: Reconciliation rows C13a and C14d (exactly one opaque call) and R5 (no second retry), in single-store and two-store mode. Needs the [relocation] extra.

title: Operator decision fenced by the ownership epoch; first decision final -> stale-epoch decision denied, identical replay deduplicated, different second decision denied, every attempt audited
notes: Reconciliation rows R1 (stale epoch), R2 (identical replay), R3 (opposite decision by a second operator) and R4 (never parked). Operator identities are unauthenticated strings.

title: False operator claim about a parked effect -> accepted and the effect is lost or duplicated (human-in-the-loop trust assumption; no exactly-once)
notes: Rows C13d (false confirmed_done: zero calls) and C14a (false confirmed_absent: two calls) document what the protocol cannot prevent; they are expected outcomes, not failures.

title: Operator reconciliation CLI -> list, decide, resume and log work end to end; denied exits 1, usage errors exit 2
notes: Also reachable as `agent-movement relocate reconcile` and `python -m agent_movement.relocation_demo reconcile`; decisions and the audit log stay in the coordinator file.

title: No unsalted content digest is stored: envelope, artifact and effect-payload digests are HMAC-SHA256 commitments under a per-store secret (raw database bytes searched for the plain SHA-256); equal inputs still commit equally within a store, so replay and conflict detection work; the secret stays out of audit exports and is never silently regenerated
notes: Issue #39. A privacy property, not an OWASP Agentic Top 10 item. The secret is in the same file, so the commitments protect exports and logs, not a copied file. The receipt returned to the sender keeps plain digests.

title: A version-1 store holding plain digests is migrated to keyed commitments in place, exactly once under process concurrency, with no plain digest left in the file or its WAL; pre-migration retries still replay identical receipts and conflicts are still detected; an unreadable stored receipt aborts the migration and leaves the file unchanged
notes: Issue #39. The concurrency test starts six OS processes on one version-1 file; a double wrap would turn every replay into a conflict. No downgrade path.

title: purge --older-than deletes the expected history rows and audits the purge, but keeps owners/epochs (fencing still refuses a stale executor), effect ledgers, revocations, in-flight admissions, parked effects awaiting reconciliation, and the admissions and uses of a grant that is still live (a single-use grant stays spent); nonces inside the floor survive; purged rows are physically erased; dry runs change nothing
notes: Issue #39. Purging deliveries ends the idempotent-retry window for them (tested). Physical erasure covers the SQLite file and its WAL, not backups. Relocation and checkpoint tables are retained, not purged.

title: Core receiver runtime revocation (signed issue #8 notice) between admission and effect commit -> the commit and every later handoff of the approval are denied, across store instances, with HS256 or a public-only Ed25519 authority
notes: Issue #38. The recheck covers tasks a HandoffReceiver delivery was admitted under; a task with no delivery is only epoch-fenced (asserted). Expiry is not rechecked at commit. No undo of committed effects.

title: Forged, unsigned, tampered, wrong-purpose, untrusted-issuer or unpinned revocation notice -> rejected (HTTP 401), audited, nothing revoked; a verified notice for an unknown approval -> 404
notes: Issue #38. HS256 authorities are symmetric: whoever holds the pinned secret can issue notices, so the receiver could revoke its own approvals; revocation only removes authority.

title: Runtime revocation is idempotent -> the same or a later notice for a revoked approval records nothing new; concurrent identical revocations record one
notes: Issue #38. The first verified notice stays the record; there is no un-revoke.

title: With receipt emission on, an applied runtime revocation is signed once as authority.revoked referencing the notice by digest, a blocked commit is a rejected tool record, and the bundle verifies
notes: Issue #38. authority.revoked is an additive receipt type of the 0.1-draft profile; refused or replayed revocations sign nothing.

title: Re-issued effect under a deterministic ID with a different payload -> rejected by the gateway; the ledger keeps the first commit (no overwrite, no duplicate)
notes: restart_stable_ids (B1-stable) in MobilityBench v0.2; fixture case neg-stable-id-divergent-payload. Simulated SQLite effects only; the restart still loses mid-session context.

title: Mid-step crash inside an effect step (before the commit, or after it is durable but before the ack) -> B0 incomplete, fresh-ID restart duplicates, deterministic-ID recovery (B1-stable, B3 failover and destination restart) commits once; a paused origin's in-flight commit is fenced
notes: The B3 tests need the relocation extra. The zombie-origin case (neg-crash-zombie-commit) runs as a v0.2 negative fixture inside the suite test. Crashes are simulated exceptions at step boundaries of one in-process interpreter, not process kills.

title: Partition between origin and destination (request dropped, reply dropped, request delayed past the sender's timeout) -> one retry; the destination deduplicates, a lost receipt is answered by a replay, never a second execution
notes: Fixture case neg-lost-receipt-replay. One fault per attempt, one retry; no message corruption, reordering beyond one late copy, or partition longer than one timeout. The A2A and B3 tests need extras.

title: MobilityBench v0.2 frozen release -> fixtures digest-verified, schedule must equal the seeded generator even under a consistent manifest; the v0.1 release and its outcomes stay byte-identical
MobilityBench v0.2 run -> byte-identical timing-free JSONL, reproducible repeats, sanitized records, explicit not-applied reasons, report with denominators and raw rows, CLI via agent-movement bench

MobilityBench v0.2 negative fixtures -> each new case passes in isolation (stable-ID conflict kept, lost receipt replayed, crashed-but-paused origin fenced, runtime revocation rejected at the effect); the static revocation flag stays a known gap
notes: The v0.1 cases keep their expectations in v0.2 (only question IDs are prefixed). Runtime revocation is the issue #38 signed-notice path; the frozen v0.1 case uses the static Approval.revoked flag.

title: Opt-in peer sender pre-disclosure gate verifies signed origin/grant, pinned destination, scope, classification and liveness before discovery and again before delivery; refuses post-admission revocation, wrong signer, downgrade and invalid settings
notes: Synthetic PeerClient.handoff only; accepted delegation still requires independent receiver/effect checks; Linux x86_64 subprocess integration is skipped on unsupported platforms; denial after disclosure is not no-disclosure.

title: Linux x86_64 separate-process seccomp/pipe-broker test rejects selected socket and spawn attempts and unsupported broker requests while enforcing trusted peer consent for one named synthetic delegation
notes: 16-case deterministic evidence plus unfenced observer control; Linux x86_64 only; no same-UID filesystem/IPC containment, general egress prohibition, direct real A2A/legacy attack or external tool guarantee.

title: Independently provisioned localhost synthetic tool service verifies signed worker and issuer grant, current owner/epoch, revocation, policy, budget and idempotency at its own SQLite effect sink; direct hostile calls, lost replies and restarts are explicitly tested
notes: Issue #102. Real localhost endpoint in a separately configured OS process, only simulated effect rows; same-UID file/IPC compromise and other tool/adapter routes are outside scope; no real external effect or cross-system exactly-once claim.

title: Root-supervised Linux x86_64 isolated synthetic worker uses distinct real/effective/saved UID/GID and no supplementary groups, root-only file/DB/proc/FD access denial, seccomp-denied socket/spawn attempts against actual legacy listener, a single trusted peer-grant broker and fail-closed timeout
notes: Issues #98 and #50. Linux x86_64 ephemeral job container root supervises nobody UID 65534; no host root; reports independently checked synthetic effects and root-only canary. Does not prove filesystem/IPC complete mediation, enabled listener suppression across other processes, integration with external tool sink or general egress containment.

title: Operator-owned broker-only secure-test profile validates a private 0600 non-symlink manifest and all reviewed 16 route classifications, launches one UID-isolated child and trusted peer broker, observes actual legacy red control and independently measured guarded peer effect/denials
notes: Issue #99. Bounded root-in-container distinct-UID broker profile, not an all-path deployment supervisor. Other independent processes can still reach legacy/A2A; tool-effect service not integrated; no global disclosure or external effect prevention claim.
